## Indicator HAL Pattern Upgrade - Complete ✅

Based on the task requirements and deviceInfo pattern analysis:

- [x] 1. Remove State enum and replace with string-based state handling
- [x] 2. Update Capabilities to use String[] for supported states
- [x] 3. Update IIndicator interface to use String instead of State enum
- [x] 4. Create IIndicatorManager interface for multi-instance support
- [x] 5. Create IIndicator interface as instance interface (with Id parcelable)
- [x] 6. Update HFP file to reflect string-based states and multi-instance capability
- [x] 7. Update CMakeLists.txt to include new files
- [x] 8. Update markdown documentation to reflect new pattern
- [x] 9. Address review feedback:
  - [x] Change HFP module name to lowercase 'indicator:'
  - [x] Update instance format to use `- Id: 0` to match code variables
  - [x] Remove UNDEFINED constant
  - [x] Remove read-only state restrictions
  - [x] Remove ERROR_UNKNOWN state
  - [x] Clarify initial state semantics (first state from HFP)
  - [x] Update copyright to 2026
  - [x] Remove redundant getPlatformCapabilities API from IIndicatorManager
  - [x] Simplify multi-instance example with single commented 2nd instance
  - [x] Clarify that all instances share the same supported states
  - [x] Fix documentation examples to match actual HFP format
- [x] 10. Run code review
- [x] 11. All changes validated

## Key Changes

### HFP Instance Format
- **Updated to `- Id: 0` format**: Changed from `- 0:` to `- Id: 0` to explicitly match the interface's `IIndicator.Id` parcelable naming convention. This establishes a new global pattern where instance identifiers use explicit field names that align with code variable names, making the HFP more readable and directly correlating with the code structure.

### Interface Simplification
- **Removed `getPlatformCapabilities()`** from `IIndicatorManager`: This API was redundant since each indicator instance already provides its own capabilities via `IIndicator.getCapabilities()`. Unlike audiosink which has platform-wide settings (mixer format/sample rate), indicator has no platform-wide configuration that differs from per-instance capabilities.

### Enhanced Documentation
- **Simplified multi-instance example**: Added a focused commented example showing one additional instance (Id: 1) for clarity.
- **Clarified state sharing**: Added explicit note that all indicator instances share the same set of supported states. Each instance can independently be set to any of these states, but the available states themselves are platform-wide and do not vary per instance.
- **Fixed documentation consistency**: Updated all documentation examples to match the actual HFP file format, using lowercase `indicator:` and `Id:` field names.

The interface now provides a cleaner API surface with consistent naming conventions throughout, establishing a pattern for future HAL modules where HFP instance definitions explicitly match interface code variable names.

prompt
You are a senior full-stack developer specializing in React, TypeScript, and modern web development.
Your task is to build a complete, production-ready podcast listening website from scratch based on the specifications in input_ui_spec.txt.
Technical Requirements
- Framework: React 18+ with TypeScript
- Styling: Tailwind CSS
- Package Manager: pnpm
- Component Library: Your choice (or custom components)
- Build Tool: Vite
Your Responsibilities
1. Read and Analyze Specification
- Read input_ui_spec.txt thoroughly
- Identify all required features
- Understand user flows and interactions
2. Generate Complete Project Structure
Create a full React + TypeScript + Tailwind project with:
- package.json with all dependencies
- tsconfig.json with proper TypeScript configuration
- tailwind.config.js with theme customization
- vite.config.ts for build configuration
- index.html as entry point
- Proper folder structure:
src/
  components/     # Reusable UI components
  pages/          # Page components
  hooks/          # Custom React hooks
  types/          # TypeScript type definitions
  utils/          # Utility functions
  data/           # Mock data
  App.tsx         # Main app component
  main.tsx        # Entry point

3. Implement All Required Features
Based on input_ui_spec.txt, you MUST implement:
- ✅ All UI pages/views mentioned
- ✅ All user interactions
- ✅ All data structures
- ✅ Responsive design (mobile + desktop)
- ✅ Proper TypeScript typing
- ✅ Component composition and reusability
- ✅ State management (useState, useContext, or external library)
- ✅ Routing (if multi-page)
4. Code Quality Standards
- TypeScript: Strict mode, no any types unless absolutely necessary
- Components: Functional components with hooks
- Styling: Tailwind utility classes, responsive design
- Accessibility: Proper ARIA labels, semantic HTML
- Performance: Lazy loading, memoization where appropriate
- Clean Code: DRY principles, proper naming, comments for complex logic
5. Generate Validation Files
validation_checklist.json
Create a comprehensive checklist:
{
  "project_setup": {
    "has_package_json": false,
    "has_tsconfig": false,
    "has_tailwind_config": false,

    "typescript_strict_mode": false,
    "no_any_types": false,
    "components_typed": false,
    "responsive_design": false,
    "accessibility_features": false
  },
  "completeness_score": 0
}

feature_matrix.json
Map spec requirements to implementation:
{
  "features": [
    {
      "id": 1,
      "name": "Feature from spec",
      "required_files": ["src/components/X.tsx", "src/pages/Y.tsx"],
      "implemented": false,
      "implementation_quality": "N/A",
      "notes": ""
    }
  ]
}

6. Generate Test Scripts
validate_project.js
A Node.js script that:
- Checks all required files exist
- Validates package.json dependencies
- Parses TypeScript files for type errors
- Checks for Tailwind classes usage
- Scans for accessibility attributes
- Validates component structure
- Generates a validation report
run_validation.sh (Linux/macOS)
#!/bin/bash
echo "Running project validation..."
node validate_project.js

run_validation.bat (Windows)
@echo off
echo Running project validation...
node validate_project.js

test_runner.js
Automated test runner that:
- Runs validation script
- Checks build success (pnpm build)
- Checks TypeScript compilation
- Generates pass/fail report with scores
- Logs to logs/validation_run.log
7. Generate README.md
Must include:
- Project overview
- Tech stack
- Installation instructions (pnpm install)
- Development server (pnpm dev)
- Build instructions (pnpm build)
- Project structure explanation
- Features implemented
- How to run validation tests
- Known limitations (if any)

This PR refines the integration of native DSFR stories into the Storybook implementation by replacing the experimental regex-based indexer with a more robust surgical wrapper generation strategy.

- Verified stories appear correctly in the Storybook sidebar under the `DSFR/` section.
- Verified that clearing Storybook cache resolves any alphabetical ordering issues.

body:
Disclaimer 
This pull request delivers a comprehensive upgrade to the LAPH codebase, focusing on critical bug fixes, security enhancements, new features, performance optimizations, and extensive documentation. The changes are fully backward compatible and significantly improve reliability, safety, and maintainability.

**Critical Bug Fixes and Security Improvements:**
- Added HTTP request timeouts and robust error handling to prevent system hangs and improve reliability. Enhanced resource management ensures temporary files are always cleaned up, even on errors. Input validation and improved error messages prevent invalid states and provide clearer feedback. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-43985e98fc34c69f11af74a4a18c7ee08adb6f4539cfee9e3d037aee7bf101f2R1-R295)

**New Features and Utilities:**
- Introduced `CodeExtractor` for intelligent extraction and validation of Python code from LLM responses, and `CodeSanitizer` for security analysis of generated code. A centralized configuration system with TOML-based execution parameters allows flexible resource and retry settings. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-deaaa9e6e5ec38dd539a1ff615c20bf63006d41ea4c787ba0e0f4eaffd979b58R1-R96) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-65ee40285ef514b5fd1e5223834ccd3dc6dadb7503561a63dd57c271dbe7c1bbR1-R91) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-27df6d473b9d2ab919f091439bcf9181da5122cd29f0411232dc3bc51f44deadR1-R29)

**Performance and Code Quality Enhancements:**
- Optimized string concatenation and enabled HTTP connection pooling for faster LLM interactions. Improved code organization, added type hints, and enhanced logging structure for better maintainability and debugging. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-43985e98fc34c69f11af74a4a18c7ee08adb6f4539cfee9e3d037aee7bf101f2R1-R295)

**Testing and Documentation:**
- Added 24 new unit and integration tests, achieving 100% test pass rate. Comprehensive documentation covers security, changelog, and improvement summaries, guiding users on configuration and best practices. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f6ed156e4bf5c791680662464b94ea5d753f219ee816b385f67870e2c0d7d4c7R1-R81) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-43985e98fc34c69f11af74a4a18c7ee08adb6f4539cfee9e3d037aee7bf101f2R1-R295)

**Configuration and Backward Compatibility:**
- New `configs/execution.toml` file enables user-customizable resource and retry limits. All changes preserve backward compatibility—no migration is required. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-27df6d473b9d2ab919f091439bcf9181da5122cd29f0411232dc3bc51f44deadR1-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154)

---

### Bug Fixes & Security
- HTTP requests now have a 300s timeout, with improved error handling and session reuse to prevent hangs and resource leaks (`core/llm_interface.py`, `core/runner.py`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-43985e98fc34c69f11af74a4a18c7ee08adb6f4539cfee9e3d037aee7bf101f2R1-R295)
- Input validation and clearer error handling for config files and GUI inputs, ensuring robust fallback and preventing invalid states (`core/repair_loop.py`, `core/prompt_manager.py`, `core/gui.py`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-43985e98fc34c69f11af74a4a18c7ee08adb6f4539cfee9e3d037aee7bf101f2R1-R295)

### New Features
- Added `CodeExtractor` utility for extracting and validating executable Python code from LLM responses (`core/code_extractor.py`).
- Introduced `CodeSanitizer` for analyzing code for dangerous operations, with configurable safety checks (`core/code_sanitizer.py`).
- Centralized configuration management with singleton pattern and TOML support (`core/config.py`, `configs/execution.toml`).

### Performance & Code Quality
- Optimized string concatenation and enabled HTTP connection pooling for improved performance, especially with large LLM outputs (`core/llm_interface.py`, `core/repair_loop.py`). [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-43985e98fc34c69f11af74a4a18c7ee08adb6f4539cfee9e3d037aee7bf101f2R1-R295)
- Improved logging structure, error categorization, and code documentation throughout the codebase. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-43985e98fc34c69f11af74a4a18c7ee08adb6f4539cfee9e3d037aee7bf101f2R1-R295)

### Testing & Documentation
- Added 24 new tests covering code extraction, execution, and sanitization, with 100% pass rate. Extensive documentation added in `SECURITY.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, and `IMPROVEMENTS_SUMMARY.md`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-f6ed156e4bf5c791680662464b94ea5d753f219ee816b385f67870e2c0d7d4c7R1-R81) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-43985e98fc34c69f11af74a4a18c7ee08adb6f4539cfee9e3d037aee7bf101f2R1-R295)

### Configuration & Compatibility
- New `configs/execution.toml` allows users to configure resource and retry limits. All changes are backward compatible; no migration required. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-27df6d473b9d2ab919f091439bcf9181da5122cd29f0411232dc3bc51f44deadR1-R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-06572a96a58dc510037d5efa622f9bec8519bc1beab13c9f251e97e657a9d4edR1-R154)Please Review my codebase & there may be merge issues to please have a look

body:
## Description

- Store OpenOCD USB-JTAG adapter serial in extension workspace state and inject it into OpenOCD startup (when available).
- When no adapter serial is stored, force OpenOCD debug level ≥ 2 on start so the serial can be discovered and persisted.
- Clear adapter serial on target changes to avoid stale device selection.
- On project configuration (profile) selection/switch:
  - Stop OpenOCD if running
  - Clear adapter serial
  - Clear adapter location (OPENOCD_USB_ADAPTER_LOCATION from idf.customExtraVars)
- Add a toggleable status bar item showing adapter binding: [Adapter] S:<serial> L:<location>
  - Controlled via ESP-IDF: Explorer (checkbox) and command palette via ESP-IDF: OpenOCD Adaptor (serial & location)
  - Highest priority among ESP-IDF status bar items when enabled
  - Clicking the [Adapter] item clears serial + location (and stops OpenOCD if running)
  - Updates live when idf.customExtraVars changes
- Add a JTAG-flash safety guard:
  - If serial or location is set → proceed with JTAG flash
  - If neither is set and multiple connected boards are detected → block and prompt user to Set Target (includes rebuild note)
  - Detection is silent (no extra progress/output spam) and best-effort (does not block if detection fails)
- Add translations and documentation entries for the new command and notifications.

## Type of change

Please delete options that are not relevant.
- Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
- New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)

## Steps to test this pull request

- **Toggle status bar item**
  - Open ESP-IDF: Explorer → Commands and enable OpenOCD Adaptor (serial & location).
  - Confirm the status bar shows: [Adapter] S:- L:- initially.

- **Set location via Set Target**
  - Run ESP-IDF: Set Espressif Device Target and pick a connected board.
  - Confirm status bar updates to show L:<...>.

- **Populate serial**
  - Start OpenOCD (or run Flash (JTAG) which prompts to launch OpenOCD if not running).
  - Confirm status bar updates to show S:<mac-like-serial> once OpenOCD logs the usb-jtag serial.

- **Clear binding via status bar click**
  - Click the [Adapter] status bar item.
  - Confirm S becomes "-" and OPENOCD_USB_ADAPTER_LOCATION is removed from idf.customExtraVars (and OpenOCD stops if it was running).

- **Project configuration switch clearing**
  - Switch Project Configuration to another profile.
  - Confirm OpenOCD is stopped and both serial + location are cleared.

- **JTAG multi-board guard**
  - Connect 2+ boards, ensure both serial and location are unset, then run Flash (JTAG).
  - Confirm you get a notification explaining the ambiguity and a Set Target action; selecting it should take you to target selection (then rebuild).

## How has this been tested?

As described above

**Test Configuration**:
* ESP-IDF Version: 5.5.1
* OS (Windows,Linux and macOS): Windows

body:
This PR addresses a critical security vulnerability where the full user object (potentially including sensitive backend fields like password hashes or internal flags) was being stored in `localStorage` and Redux state.

**Changes:**
1.  **New Utility:** Created `src/shared/utils/security.js` with `sanitizeUser` function that implements a whitelist approach (allowing only `id`, `username`, `email`, `first_name`, `last_name`, `phone_number`, `role`, `is_active`).
2.  **Service Layer:** Updated `src/shared/services/authService.js` to use `sanitizeUser` before persisting to `localStorage`.
3.  **State Management:** Updated `src/features/authentication/authSlice.js` to sanitize payloads for `login`, `register`, `fetchProfile`, and `updateProfile` actions.
4.  **UI Layer:** Updated `src/features/authentication/LoginForm.jsx` to use sanitized data when dispatching actions and calling services.
5.  **Tests:** Added `src/shared/utils/security.test.js` to verify whitelisting logic.

**Impact:**
Prevents "Mass Assignment" vulnerabilities from leaking into client-side storage, ensuring that even if the API returns excessive data, the client only persists what is safe and necessary.

Users needed a centralized reference for configuring API keys across reconnaissance tools, with clarity on which services offer free tiers versus paid-only options, and the ability to enter and save keys directly in the GUI. Additionally, reports needed to persist permanently instead of disappearing when scans complete. ## Changes ### API Keys Management Added new "API Keys" tab in Settings between "Tool Toggles" and "Concurrency" containing: - **Interactive form with input fields** for all 8 API providers: - Amass: Shodan, VirusTotal, SecurityTrails, Censys, PassiveTotal, BinaryEdge, BeVigil - Subfinder: GitHub Personal Access Token - **Visual badges** (FREE TIER, PAID ONLY, FREE) for quick identification - **Per-provider details**: Service description, rate limits, cost breakdown, direct registration links - **GUI functionality**: - Text input fields for entering API keys - Automatically loads existing keys from config files when tab opens - "Save API Keys" button updates both Amass and Subfinder configs - Success/error status messages after saving - **Backend API endpoints**: - `GET /api/api-keys` - Retrieves current keys from config files - `POST /api/api-keys` - Saves keys to both config files - **Cost transparency**: - 7 services with free tiers (100-5000 queries/month) - 1 paid-only service (BinaryEdge, $10/month minimum) - Paid plan pricing for upgrade decisions - **Pro tips section**: Optimal free tier combinations, GitHub token recommendation ### Persistent Reports Display Enhanced the Reports section to display completed scans permanently: - **Backend modifications**: - Modified `build_state_payload()` to merge completed jobs from `completed_jobs.json` with active targets - Completed job data converted to target format for display - Completion timestamps preserved and added to target metadata - **Frontend enhancements**: - Completed reports show "Complete" badge with completion timestamp - Active/pending scans show "Pending" badge - Timestamp displayed as "Completed: [date/time]" below report cards - All historical reconnaissance data remains accessible - **Persistence guarantee**: - Reports never disappear when scans finish - Data from `state.json` (active) and `completed_jobs.json` (completed) merged automatically - All past scan results, subdomains, and vulnerabilities remain visible ## Implementation **Backend Functions (API Keys):** - Parses INI format (`~/.config/amass/config.ini`) and YAML format (`~/.config/subfinder/provider-config.yaml`) - Creates config files if they don't exist - Automatically copies shared keys to both tools **Backend Functions (Reports):** - Loads completed jobs from `recon_data/completed_jobs.json` - Merges with active targets from `recon_data/state.json` - Adds completion timestamps to display - Active targets take precedence when domains overlap **Frontend:** - Form with 8 input fields that load existing values - JavaScript handles API calls to load/save keys - Real-time feedback on save operations - Reports display completion timestamps for finished scans ## Example Config Files ```ini # ~/.config/amass/config.ini [datasources.shodan] [datasources.shodan.Credentials] apikey = YOUR_SHODAN_KEY_HERE [datasources.virustotal] [datasources.virustotal.Credentials] apikey = YOUR_VIRUSTOTAL_KEY_HERE ``` ```yaml # ~/.config/subfinder/provider-config.yaml github: [YOUR_GITHUB_TOKEN_HERE] shodan: [YOUR_SHODAN_KEY_HERE] ``` ## Screenshots **API Keys Form:** **Reports with Persistent History:** ## Technical Notes - Integrates with existing settings tab system - API endpoints follow existing patterns - Links open in new tabs to official provider sites - No manual file editing required - Shared provider keys automatically synced between tools - Reports persist across page reloads and remain accessible indefinitely - Completion timestamps help track scan history

body:
Overview: This pull request deletes the automated research bot scaffolding and its dependencies from the repository. Specifically, it removes prof_mackson_prompt.json, run_prof_mackson.py, and requirements.txt, effectively eliminating the autonomous, daily-research workflow that previously generated topics, outlines, full articles, and email summaries.

What changed:
- Deleted prof_mackson_prompt.json: The autonomous prompt/configuration used to drive the research bot.
- Deleted run_prof_mackson.py: The daily automation script that generated topics, outlines, articles, and email reports.
- Deleted requirements.txt: Removed SDKs and libraries (e.g., Google Gen AI, schedule) tied to the automated workflow.

Rationale:
- The automated system introduced a self-contained content-generation loop that attempted to autonomously crawl literature, synthesize sources, and produce publishable material. This raises concerns about reliability, reproducibility, and academic integrity, and it depends on external services and credentials not suitable for a passive codebase.
- Removing these components reduces security and maintenance risks, avoids embedding external API dependencies in the repository, and keeps the project focused on manual, high-quality literature review and writing processes.

Impact:
- No code execution or automated content generation is available in the repo anymore.
- No external API keys or secrets are stored or referenced in the repository.
- The project now relies on manual literature review and authoring processes, following the provided outline and research design guidelines.

What to do next:
- Follow the Literature Review outline described in the issue prompt, focusing on conducting a critical synthesis, systematic analysis of EFL gamification in Libyan context, and Al-Ajelat Primary Schools setting.
- Source at least four Libyan-related references (preferably 2000–2025) with APA-style citations and DOIs where available. Include direct quotations with page numbers where relevant.
- Build the literature review and research sections manually, ensuring academic rigor and cohesive narrative without reliance on automated generation.

Testing guidance:
- Confirm that prof_mackson_prompt.json, run_prof_mackson.py, and requirements.txt are removed from the repository.
- Search the repo to verify there are no remaining references to the removed files or Google Gen AI/schedule dependencies.

Future considerations:
- If an automated workflow is reintroduced, implement it with strict governance: validated sources, explicit data provenance, citation traceability, and safeguards for ethical research practices. Include clear documentation on how to configure and run the automation locally, and ensure all outputs are clearly authored and cited.

author: guillep
body:
Add support for instead hook.

The instead hook works alone, it is by design combined with before/after.
If you apply the instead  hook, you should apply the before and after altogether, in that single hook.
That is, the before/after hooks are ignored even if defined.

This leaves us with four different instrumentation variants.
 - before only, then forward to normal method
 - after only, forwarding to normal method
 - before and after around forwarding to normal method
 - instead of normal method


Depends on #38

author: davidorme
body:
# Description

> [!TIP]
> This is a repeat of #564, which was accidentally merged down into #555 not `develop`. 
> 
> The original PR was forked off #555 as a demo, but #555 was closed before this one, so the merge was down into a dead branch. This is now targeted at `develop` instead.

This PR:

* Adds the new `core.datasets` module providing the `get_pyrealm_data` command and some supporting objects and commands.
* Links to the `ipynb` files automatically generated during the `sphinx` build using the `download` role. This replaces the statically maintained parallel `ipynb` versions we had before.
* Replaces the `importlib` stuff in the workbooks to get files with the more portable `get_pyrealm_data` command.
* Processes the automatically generated `ipynb` file to strip out `jupytext` settings. These are a problem if a user _does_ have `jupyter-lab` with `jupytext` as the `ipynb` format is not included in our `jupytext` settings (we only use markdown notebooks in the docs source) and `jupytext` objects to what it sees as a rogue format.

TODO - currently no testing. To do a sensible job, we'd probably need to mock the `pooch.Pooch.fetch` calls (and probably provides some way to set the cache directory rather than just using the system cache within tests).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> We still need to decide when to run the `core.datasets._populate_pooch_registry()` method?
> 
> This automatically creates the links that `pooch` uses to get the raw objects from `repo` - it's only _really_ needed when a new release is made. It seems like overkill to run it on every commit. We can run it as:
>
>  ```sh
>  python -m pyrealm.core.datasets
>  ```

Fixes #563

**JIRA** → [BAH-4298](https://bahmni.atlassian.net/browse/BAH-4298)

Patient relationship search ComboBox was not accepting complete patient IDs. For example, when entering ID "ABC200036", the input would only accept up to "ABC20003" with characters disappearing during typing.

The handlePatientSearch function was calling updateRelationship to set patientId on every keystroke. This caused a conflict between the ComboBox's internal input state (what the user types) and the controlled React state, making characters disappear.

Removed the updateRelationship call from handlePatientSearch in usePatientRelationship.ts
- The patientId is now only set when a patient is selected from the dropdown (through handlePatientSelect)
- During typing, only search terms are tracked, allowing the ComboBox to manage its input freely

## Description

Add the option to use `-c` in the install script to specify the client that is doing the installation. This is defaulted to install-script, but allows for the setup-trivy github action to specify -c gh-action or something similar when installing to help differentiate in the logs

An allow list of acceptable clients will be added to trivy-downloads to filter spurious entries

Without client specified (defaults to install-script):

body:
This pull request introduces several improvements to the order creation workflow, focusing on enhancing the service mode selection, coupon application logic, and invoice PDF generation. The main changes include refactoring the service mode ComboBox to use data binding and observable collections, improving coupon UI logic, and updating the PDF invoice table rendering for clarity and maintainability.

**Order creation and service mode enhancements:**

* Refactored the service mode ComboBox in `CreateOrderView.xaml` to bind to `ViewModel.ServiceModes` and `ViewModel.SelectedServiceMode`, enabling dynamic updates and better MVVM compliance. The selection logic in the code-behind was updated to work with string values instead of `ComboBoxItem` objects, and initialization now ensures the correct mode is selected based on the view model. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a155ba54acc4b71742e7a4829ca0663eb3f7ba4930f6f343774b419c9b73a0adL338-R346) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8bdd1be60ad4dc6418b6a4426904a8659a5be8b51c9e59b56c75fc67d1491e78R112-R117) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-8bdd1be60ad4dc6418b6a4426904a8659a5be8b51c9e59b56c75fc67d1491e78R454) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-8bdd1be60ad4dc6418b6a4426904a8659a5be8b51c9e59b56c75fc67d1491e78R471-R473) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-1f499fd7888de70543d561f2ad0dde36c385b75408578b1795034b06e47e786eR112-R123) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-1f499fd7888de70543d561f2ad0dde36c385b75408578b1795034b06e47e786eL161-R174) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-1f499fd7888de70543d561f2ad0dde36c385b75408578b1795034b06e47e786eL171-L185)
* Added logic to move the selected service mode to the top of the `ServiceModes` collection in the view model, ensuring the most recently selected mode is prioritized in the UI.

**Coupon application improvements:**

* Introduced the `IsApplyVisible` property in the view model to control the visibility of the Apply button, which now appears only when a coupon code is entered and not yet applied. Updated the XAML to use this new property for button visibility. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8bdd1be60ad4dc6418b6a4426904a8659a5be8b51c9e59b56c75fc67d1491e78L61-R72) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-a155ba54acc4b71742e7a4829ca0663eb3f7ba4930f6f343774b419c9b73a0adL711-R723)
* Enhanced the coupon suggestion box UI by limiting the dropdown height and simplifying the logic for filtering and displaying coupon suggestions. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-a155ba54acc4b71742e7a4829ca0663eb3f7ba4930f6f343774b419c9b73a0adR682-R688) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-1f499fd7888de70543d561f2ad0dde36c385b75408578b1795034b06e47e786eL268-L274) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-1f499fd7888de70543d561f2ad0dde36c385b75408578b1795034b06e47e786eL297-R313)

**Invoice PDF rendering:**

* Updated the PDF invoice generation to use `RelativeItem` instead of `RelativeColumn` for table headers and rows, aligning with the latest document rendering API and ensuring better layout consistency.

author: adarsh-priydarshi-5646
body:
### Proposed Changes

Fixes #14827

- Fixed memory leak caused by inline arrow function in `ended` event listener
- Created `handleEnded` callback using `useCallback` to maintain stable function reference
- Updated `addEventListener` and `removeEventListener` to use the same `handleEnded` reference for proper cleanup

**Problem:**

The `ended` event listener was using an inline arrow function `() => setIsPlaying(false)`, which created a new function reference on each render. This caused `removeEventListener` to fail silently because it received a different function reference than what was passed to `addEventListener`.

**Solution:**
```tsx
const handleEnded = useCallback(() => {
  setIsPlaying(false);
}, []);

audio.addEventListener("ended", handleEnded);
audio.removeEventListener("ended", handleEnded); // Same reference ✓

```

Add `kaspa-tools sim roundtrip` command for single roundtrip testing (deposit from Kaspa to Hub, then withdraw back) that properly reuses existing infrastructure instead of duplicating code.

author: dpgeorge
body:
### Summary

During the discussion about t-string support #17557, I thought that it might not be much effort to support nested f-strings with the current f-string parser.  And it turned out relatively simple.

The way the MicroPython f-string parser works is:
1. it extracts the f-string arguments (things in curly braces) into a temporary buffer (a vstr)
2. once the f-string ends (reaches its closing quote) the lexer switches to tokenizing the temporary buffer
3. once the buffer is empty it switches back to the stream.

The temporary buffer can easily hold f-strings itself (ie nested f-strings) and they can be re-parsed by the lexer using the same algorithm.  The only thing stopping that from working is that the temporary buffer can't be reused for the nested f-string because it's currently being parsed.

This PR fixes that by adding a second temporary buffer, which is the "injection" buffer.  That allows arbitrary number of nestings with a simple modification to the original algorithm:
1. when an f-string is encountered the string is parsed and its arguments are extracted into `fstring_args`
2. when the f-string finishes, `fstring_args` is inserted into the current position in `inject_chrs` (which is the start of that buffer if no injection is ongoing)
3. `fstring_args` is now cleared and ready for any further f-strings (nested or not)
4. the lexer switches to `inject_chrs` if it's not already reading from it
5. if an f-string appeared inside the f-string then it is in `inject_chrs` and can be processed as before, extracting its arguments into `fstring_args`, which can then be inserted again into `inject_chrs`
6. once `inject_chrs` is exhausted (meaning that all levels of f-strings have been fully processed) the lexer switched back to tokenizing the stream

Amazingly, this scheme supports arbitrary numbers of nestings of f-strings using the same quote style.

### Testing

A new test is added which will run under CI.

### Trade-offs and Alternatives

This adds some code size and a bit more memory usage for the lexer.  In particular for a single (non-nested) f-string it now makes an extra copy of the `fstring_args` data, when copying it across to `inject_chrs`.  That could possibly be optimized to reuse the same buffer (`inject_chrs` would steal the memory from `fstring_args`).

Otherwise, memory use only goes up with the complexity of nested f-strings.

body:
# Description#

- This PR introduces a configurable option to delay the permanent deletion of RBD volumes by moving them to the RBD trash with a specified deferment time.
- 
- Previously, the CSI driver invoked `rbdImage.Trash(0)` with a hard-coded deferment value of `0`, meaning deleted volumes were immediately eligible for purge or removal depending on the backend configuration. There was no way to specify a delay from the CSI side to allow recovery of accidentally deleted volumes.
- 
- This change allows administrators to configure a safety window (for example, one hour) during which deleted volumes remain in the RBD trash and can be recovered before being permanently removed.


## Is there anything that requires special attention ##
- No special attention is required for normal usage.

Do you have any questions?
- No open questions at this time.

Is the change backward compatible?
Yes, the change is backward compatible.

Are there concerns around backward compatibility?
No. The default value of the new configuration is `0`, which preserves the existing behavior.

Provide any external context for the change, if any.
- This change aligns with Ceph RBD’s native support for trash deferment.
- It allows Ceph-CSI users to better leverage Ceph’s safety mechanisms when managing persistent volumes in Kubernetes environments.
- No CSI spec changes are required for this enhancement.

## Related issues ##

Mention any github issues relevant to this PR. Adding below line
will help to auto close the issue once the PR is merged.

Fixes: #5830 

## Tests Performed

- Attempted local execution of RBD unit tests:
  - go test ./internal/rbd/...

  These fail locally due to missing Ceph native libraries
  (librbd, librados), required by go-ceph CGO bindings.

- Attempted CGO-disabled execution:
  - CGO_ENABLED=0 go test ./internal/rbd/features

  This fails as expected because feature detection relies on
  CGO-enabled Ceph symbols.

- Provided a detailed validation guide describing how to
  verify the behavior in a Ceph-backed Kubernetes environment.

Full verification is expected to be covered by CI.

author: policyengine[bot]
body:
## Problem

Testing the deployed API after PR #13 revealed two critical issues preventing the MCP workflow:

### 1. Search functionality broken
The `/parameters` endpoint had `@cache(expire=3600)` which cached results without considering query parameters. Searching for `?search=basic_rate` returned all parameters instead of filtered results.

### 2. Missing core UK parameters  
The seeding script filtered parameters to only include those with labels:
```python
parameters_to_add = [p for p in model_version.parameters if p.label is not None]
```

This excluded fundamental UK tax system parameters like `gov.hmrc.income_tax.rates.uk[0].rate`. The database only had 82 UK parameters (mostly contrib/* policy levers), making the workflow incomplete.

## Solution

**Cache fix**: Removed the `@cache` decorator from the parameters endpoint. The search parameter is now properly respected.

**Seeding fix**: Changed to seed ALL parameters:
```python
parameters_to_add = model_version.parameters
```

This ensures core tax system parameters are available for policy creation.

## Testing needed

After deployment:
1. Verify search works: `/parameters/?search=basic_rate` should return filtered results
2. Check UK parameters: Run `make db-reset-prod && make seed` to re-seed with all parameters
3. Complete the workflow: Search for basic_rate → create policy → run analysis

## Note

The production database will need to be re-seeded after this PR merges to get the missing parameters.

# Summary

Adding support for [ExternalArtifact](https://fluxcd.io/flux/components/source/externalartifacts/) as an ArtifactGenerator source.

Fixes #259.

# Changes

- Updates ArtifactGenerator API to accept ExternalArtifact as source.
- Updates ArtifactGenerator Controller to handle ExternalArtifact source.

# Testing

1. Deploying controller in kind cluster:
```bash
kind create cluster
make dev-deploy
make docker-build
kind load docker-image fluxcd/source-watcher:latest
```

2. Create GitRepository as initial source:
```yaml
---
apiVersion: source.toolkit.fluxcd.io/v1
kind: GitRepository
metadata:
  name: podinfo
  namespace: default
spec:
  interval: 5m0s
  url: https://github.com/stefanprodan/podinfo
  ref:
    branch: master
```

3. Create ArtifactGenerator to generate an ExternalArtifact from the GitRepo:

apiVersion: source.extensions.fluxcd.io/v1beta1
kind: ArtifactGenerator
metadata:

spec:
  sources:
    - alias: podinfo
      kind: GitRepository
      name: podinfo
  artifacts:
    - name: my-app-composite
      copy:
        - from: "@podinfo/**"
          to: "@artifact/my-app/"

### What does this PR do?
This pull request introduces four new status-based endpoints for the `sites` resource to align with the existing device status endpoints. This allows clients to query sites based on their operational status in a more intuitive way.

The new endpoints are:
- `/api/v2/devices/sites/status/operational`
- `/api/v2/devices/sites/status/transmitting`
- `/api/v2/devices/sites/status/data-available`
- `/api/v2/devices/sites/status/not-transmitting`

### Why is this change needed?
To maintain API consistency and provide a standardized method for filtering sites by their online and data transmission status, mirroring the functionality recently implemented for devices.

author: neworderofjamie
body:
For some reason or other, CUDA 13 deprecates some vector types like ``double4``. However, these continue to be used in cuRAND via some sort of deprecation-ignoring mechanism. It _looks_ like this is being applied incorrectly in ``curand_normal4_double`` causing compiler errors when you try and build the CUDA backend against CUDA 13 using Visual Studio (see #723).

This _could_ be a CUDA bug (I have filed an issue with NVIDIA) or, by including ``curand_kernel.h`` in host code to  get the size of some device types, we might be doing something sketchy. Either way, this PR solves the issue by blanket ignoring the deprecation of vector types.

body:
## Summary

This PR improves UI consistency across the application by replacing hardcoded background colors with CSS variables and enhances button states and pagination logic. These changes improve theming support and provide better visual feedback for user interactions.

## Changes

- **Replace hardcoded colors with CSS variables**: Changed `bg-white` to `bg-background` across multiple components (contact form, newsletter, navigation, pricing cards, news articles, contact persons, group cards, and email templates)
- **Improve pagination calculation**: Fixed pagination logic to correctly account for START_INDEX offset when determining if there's a next page
- **Enhance button states**: Added `data-disabled` attributes to arrow buttons for better styling control and improved disabled state visual feedback with opacity and cursor styles
- **Improve button hover states**: Increased button hover opacity from 50% to 80% for better visibility
- **Enhance group card styling**: Updated group card hover state to use primary color and added border to icon for better visual definition
- **Reorganize CSS utilities**: Moved `btn--sm` utility class for better organization

## Motivation

Using hardcoded `bg-white` throughout the application prevents proper theming support and makes it difficult to maintain consistent design system values. By replacing these with the `bg-background` CSS variable, we enable better theme support and ensure consistency across the application. Additionally, the pagination fix ensures users can properly navigate through all available content, and the improved button states provide clearer visual feedback for disabled interactions.

author: reuvendagaga
body:
CRITICAL BUG FIX: Gate enhancements were stored but not applied!

Problem:
- User shot 20 bullets at -3 gate
- Still lost 3 soldiers (no enhancement applied)
- Enhancement was being stored in React state
- But state updates are ASYNC in React
- When player passed through gate immediately after shooting
- handleGateTrigger read from state, but state not updated yet
- So enhancement was always 0!

Root cause: React state closure issue
- gateEnhancements is a state variable
- State updates don't happen immediately
- handleGateTrigger reads stale state value
- Classic React async state problem

Solution: Use REF + STATE together
- gateEnhancementsRef: Updated IMMEDIATELY when bullets hit
- gateEnhancements (state): Updated for React re-renders (visuals)
- handleGateTrigger: Reads from REF for instant access
- Both cleared together after gate trigger

Now working correctly:
✅ Shoot 20 bullets at -3 gate → enhancement = 20
✅ Pass through gate → reads enhancement = 20 from ref ✅ Effect: -3 + 20 = +17 soldiers gained!
✅ Gate text shows +17 when hit by 20 bullets
✅ No more async state issues

Test: Shoot many bullets at negative gate, should gain soldiers instead!

body:
💡 **What:**
- Modified `AddRecentMessage` in `pkg/memory/surreal_store.go` to run the deletion query only 10% of the time.
- Updated `GetRecentMessages` to `LIMIT 20` and `ORDER BY timestamp DESC`, then reverse the result in Go.
- Fixed `pkg/bot/memory_processing_test.go` to use the correct `HandlerConfig` struct for `NewHandler`.

🎯 **Why:**
- The previous implementation executed a complex `DELETE` with a subquery on *every single message insert*, doubling the database load for chat operations.
- This created a potential bottleneck as message volume increases.

📊 **Impact:**
- Reduces database write operations for message history by ~90%.
- Maintains read performance at O(1) via strict `LIMIT` on reads.
- `GetRecentMessages` now robustly handles cases where the table temporarily exceeds the target size.

🔬 **Measurement:**
- Verified via `go test ./pkg/memory/...` (updated tests to allow flexible message count <= 20).
- Verified `go test ./pkg/bot/...` passes with updated constructor usage.

body:
Completed the final stage of Phase 3 (Full Swap).
Key achievements:
1.  **VM Logic Swap**: The VM now performs integer, float, and string operations by reading operands directly from the custom memory allocator (`memory.Read*`). This proves that the system's operational data is residing in the custom arena, reducing reliance on the Go GC for value storage.
2.  **Safety**: Added `ensureOnHeap` to automatically allocate memory for literals and constants before use, preventing null pointer issues in arrays and operations.
3.  **Scheduler**: Added `Worker` struct and loop logic to consume tasks from the FIFO queue.
4.  **Verification**: All VM tests passed with the new memory-read logic.

author: alexggh
body:
## Work in progress

## Description

Implements the proposed changes from here https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/pull/10452, where the API surface has been limited to two functions `submit` and a `subscribe_statement`.

### Submit changes 

For submitting the only changes are implementing the logic of the newly `expiry` field where statements with an expiration timestamp lower than current time get rejected.

### Subscribe changes

For subscription the approach is to have a configurable number of workers that keep track of all subscriptions, each time a new subscription arrives it gets assigned by a round-robin protocol to one of the workers.

When a new statements gets accepted by the statement-store it notifies all workers about the statement, the workers then go and evaluate all subscription filters they are assigned to and notifies each of them accordingly. 

## Remaining work
- [x] Add more tests.
- [x] Evaluate performance under load and port `statement_store_bench.rs` to using subscribe API, ported and performance stay the same on the benchmark, because bottlenecks are elsewhere and being addressed.
```
[2026-01-07T17:18:51Z INFO  tests::zombie_ci::statement_store_bench] Participants: 49998, each sent: 6, received: 0
[2026-01-07T17:18:51Z INFO  tests::zombie_ci::statement_store_bench] Summary        min       avg       max
[2026-01-07T17:18:51Z INFO  tests::zombie_ci::statement_store_bench]  time, s         8        19        24
[2026-01-07T17:18:51Z INFO  tests::zombie_ci::statement_store_bench]  retries         0         0         0
```

- [x] Evaluate and set proper RPC limits. The normal RPC limits apply here  we just need to make sure RPC nodes run with limits high enough, so each user can connect to the node all at the same time.
- [x] Periodically scan existing statements and removed expired ones.
- [ ] Plan for deploying it with minimising impact for people prototype with the old APIs
  - [ ]  ~This modifies statement format(expiry field), Runtime and Node need to run latest version.~, post https://github.com/paritytech/polkadot-sdk/pull/10787, statement-store does not call into runtime anymore, so this dependency is not needed.

## Local testing

To obtain a local node with the new APIs available run:
  
  ```
  cargo build -p polkadot -p polkadot-parachain-bin  --bin polkadot --bin polkadot-prepare-worker --bin polkadot-execute-worker --bin polkadot-parachain  --features fast-runtime;
   
  ZOMBIE_PROVIDER=native cargo test -p cumulus-zombienet-sdk-tests --features zombie-ci zombie_ci::statement_store::statement_store
  ```
  
  The rpc addresses are visible in the output:
  ```
  charlie: direct link (pjs) https://polkadot.js.org/apps/?rpc=ws://127.0.0.1:26997#/explorer
  dave: direct link (pjs) https://polkadot.js.org/apps/?rpc=ws://127.0.0.1:12623#/explorer
  ```

author: copilot
body:
When adding a player to a team, a NullPointerException occurs if the team reload from database fails. The error manifests at two points: `loadTeamPlayers()` attempting to call `team.getName()` on null, and `handleAddPlayer()` attempting to call `selectedTeam.getName()` on null after a failed reload.

## Changes

**`reloadSelectedTeamFromDatabase()` (line 920)**
- Return `boolean` to signal success/failure instead of void
- Add null checks in team lookup loop
- Preserve existing `selectedTeam` reference on failure instead of leaving it in undefined state

**`loadTeamPlayers()` (line 705)**
- Add null guard at method entry to handle null team parameter gracefully

**`handleAddPlayer()` (line 456)**
- Check reload return value and exit early with user warning if reload fails
- Prevents accessing null `selectedTeam` reference

## Example

Before:
```java
reloadSelectedTeamFromDatabase(); // void return, no failure indication
showAlert("Success", "Player added to " + selectedTeam.getName()); // NPE if reload failed
```

After:
```java
if (!reloadSelectedTeamFromDatabase()) {
    showAlert("Warning", "Player added but team data could not be refreshed");
    return;
}
showAlert("Success", "Player added to " + selectedTeam.getName()); // safe
```

body:
Replace string contains() assertions with exact pattern matching
against structured error types. This makes tests more robust by:

- Matching error variants explicitly (e.g., SemanticError::CopyableError)
- Comparing exact field values instead of substring matching
- Using helper functions to extract identifiers from formatted strings

Tests refactored:
- will_fail_on_an_extern_without_size: MissingExternAttribute
- 6 copyable error tests: CopyableError
- 1 cloneable error test: CloneableError
- 4 defaultable error tests: DefaultableError, EnumDefaultableMissingDefault, EnumDefaultWithoutDefaultable
- 1 size mismatch test: SizeMismatch
- 2 bitflags tests: BitflagsDefaultableMissingDefault, BitflagsDefaultWithoutDefaultable, BitflagsInvalidType
- 1 vftable mismatch test: VftableFunctionMismatch with exact function name extraction

author: janne6565
body:
This pull request introduces significant enhancements to access management and entity modeling in the backend. The main changes are the addition of fine-grained, annotation-based access control on controller endpoints, the introduction of a new `Action` enum to support this, and improvements to the invite and user role systems. Additionally, some logging levels and code organization have been updated for clarity and maintainability.

**Access Management Enhancements:**

* Introduced the `Action` enum to represent CRUD operations for access management, enabling more granular permission checks.
* Applied the `@RequireAccess` annotation to controller endpoints in `GameServerConfigurationController`, `UserEntityController`, and `UserInviteController`, specifying required actions (CREATE, READ, DELETE) and resources for each endpoint. The `@ResourceId` annotation is now used on relevant path variables. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-e2c613d8f321699500af0a689bebb0490878307b2b8ad9462d9be4940e66e564R29) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e2c613d8f321699500af0a689bebb0490878307b2b8ad9462d9be4940e66e564L34-R60) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-faf31352ad848ced36ed93750de275ef7ab0dd2284af1051101c93068cdf0786R25) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-faf31352ad848ced36ed93750de275ef7ab0dd2284af1051101c93068cdf0786L28-R42) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-2b9693ebd769daccb70737dbeb6c7a4c347142ce985e80eefe2870d6ab96f6e5R34) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-2b9693ebd769daccb70737dbeb6c7a4c347142ce985e80eefe2870d6ab96f6e5R50) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-2b9693ebd769daccb70737dbeb6c7a4c347142ce985e80eefe2870d6ab96f6e5R72)

**User and Invite Role Improvements:**

* Added a `role` field to `UserInviteCreationDto`, `UserInviteDto`, and `UserInviteEntity`, allowing invites to specify the role of the invited user. The `UserEntity.Role` enum now includes an `ADMIN` value. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-5d8fad7fffe04b5d8506cd5e3ad0088f9b17e2b3dc08ca81ddef3890b507457dR6-R14) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-64de6b9b0efee4e155776d4f1ab087658c0e451240603ad068e364f3d0985e8eR25) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-ddd875c4827812e39109c9517a0bbbf431545269dd983b982257df270d1d98bbR40-R42) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-ddd875c4827812e39109c9517a0bbbf431545269dd983b982257df270d1d98bbR51) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-d4ece9575de3f02b3e227d7f832a3f9cff0bd63352cd76aa0f3ec1464a43d954R42)
* Updated the invite creation logic to accept the full `UserInviteCreationDto` (including role) instead of just a username.

**Entity and DTO Refactoring:**

* Added a `toEntity()` method to `GameServerCreationDto` for cleaner conversion to `GameServerConfigurationEntity`, and updated the controller to use this method. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8b0a36d3b71194704d05ad6a422e3080ef7399755c400fa3873f8793076eccd4R44-R65) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e2c613d8f321699500af0a689bebb0490878307b2b8ad9462d9be4940e66e564L34-R60)
* Improved import organization and code formatting in several files for clarity. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8bfaabde951d036cffee5db7e24604afdcd6db062b0bccdbd6ab9f3f592ddb7fL5-L6) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-e2c613d8f321699500af0a689bebb0490878307b2b8ad9462d9be4940e66e564L7-R19) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-faf31352ad848ced36ed93750de275ef7ab0dd2284af1051101c93068cdf0786R5-R16) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-2b9693ebd769daccb70737dbeb6c7a4c347142ce985e80eefe2870d6ab96f6e5R9-R23) [[5]](diffhunk://#diff-8b0a36d3b71194704d05ad6a422e3080ef7399755c400fa3873f8793076eccd4R6-R15) [[6]](diffhunk://#diff-64de6b9b0efee4e155776d4f1ab087658c0e451240603ad068e364f3d0985e8eL6-R10) [[7]](diffhunk://#diff-9ea4dd2f4d7db5f819319d8843d6b99cb14fb0f7b2f33af1cdd0d4c85ba40fa1R10-L12) [[8]](diffhunk://#diff-d4ece9575de3f02b3e227d7f832a3f9cff0bd63352cd76aa0f3ec1464a43d954L5-R8) [[9]](diffhunk://#diff-ddd875c4827812e39109c9517a0bbbf431545269dd983b982257df270d1d98bbL7-R12)

**Logging and Error Handling:**

* Changed logging levels from `warn` to `debug` in `GlobalExceptionHandler` for less noisy logs during normal error handling. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-8bfaabde951d036cffee5db7e24604afdcd6db062b0bccdbd6ab9f3f592ddb7fR17-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-8bfaabde951d036cffee5db7e24604afdcd6db062b0bccdbd6ab9f3f592ddb7fL40-R41)

These changes collectively improve security, maintainability, and the flexibility of user and resource management in the backend.

author: p-strusiewiczsurmacki-mobica
body:
This PR fixes #1287 

It turned out that the issue described by @Cellebyte did occur not only for dualstack services, but all -  kube-vip tried to delete the service in two codepaths if service election was enabled. I've changed where service is tagged as inactive and in what circumstances should be delete called, so the `unable to find/stop service` log should not be displayed now.

Additionally added  service's UID to some logs to ease service tracking a bit and updated the titles of BGP e2e tests to be more distinguishable.

v2.4.0 
# v2.4.0

## Highlights

Welcome to the release `v2.4.0` of Immich. This release focuses on bug fixes, QoL improvements, and polished UI components and animation across mobile and the web. Let’s dive right in.

* Show the owner's name in the shared album
* Command palette
* Change search type directly in the search bar
* Better action button placement in the mobile asset viewer
* Notable fix: fix an issue where metadata extraction could fail on high concurrency

### Show the owner's name in the shared album.

On the web, in shared albums, you can now toggle an option to display the asset’s owner name at the bottom right corner of the thumbnail.

<img width="800" alt="asset owner name in album" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/90f425b3-91d4-4ef3-9455-234b2c28b0f0" />

### Command palette

The web app now has an integrated command palette, which can be opened  `ctrl + k` on Windows/Linux or `cmd + k` on macOS. This first iteration of this lets you quickly navigate between administration pages by typing the name of the page you want to go to. It also already supports some common actions when on the respective admin pages, many of which also support shortcuts. Have a look around and check them out! 

<img width="800"  alt="command pallet" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e9fb1638-a926-4df2-92ce-3ddfd0b04e02" />


### Change search type directly in the search bar

You can now click on the pill from the search bar to select a different search type without opening the search filter panel.

<img width="800" alt="search type" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/493d0b74-8b6f-4581-b2ba-9f00da9bcc30" />


### Better placement of action buttons in the mobile asset viewer

Previously, to perform a specific action on the asset, you needed first to swipe up to open the detail panel, then swipe all the way to the right and tap the action. It limits the discoverability of some actions. To help resolve that issue, all the action buttons in the detail panel are now moved to the drop-down menu when tapping on the vertical dot icon (or kebab menu), along with some buttons that used to be on the top bar, clearing up space to display more helpful information when viewing the asset.

 <img width="350" alt="kebab menu" src="https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7b4610c4-d04b-4f5e-8b7b-02504a9ee531" />

author: calvinbayer
body:
### What does this PR do?
This PR removes a condition that causes the Datadog backend not to be queried for advanced feature settings in case a kill-switch for ITR is provided through the environment variables.

### Motivation
In the past, ITR was the only advanced feature, so calling the endpoint to receive feature configuration wasn't necessary with the kill-switch being provided. With more advanced features being added, this causes unwanted side-effects - users might want to toggle off ITR through environment variables but use other features that are being toggled on using the backend request.
In other tracers, this logic was already removed in the past, e.g., [dd-trace-py](https://github.com/DataDog/dd-trace-py/pull/12780/files)

This commit changes the Hyperlight API so that every sandbox is created from a snapshot. This is useful for several reasons; most immediately, in the same commit, note that it allows us to avoid precommitting to a size for the page table region, so we no longer need to estimate that region's size.

This PR also makes the `map_region` function private so that all the new types related to paging do not have to be exposed publicly, whilst this function is used by hyperlight-wasm, it needs to be updated to use simpler public types.

author: win5923
body:
## Description

 When the autoscaler attempts to terminate QUEUED instances to enforce the `max_num_nodes_per_type` limit, the reconciler crashes with an assertion error. This happens because QUEUED instances are selected for termination, but the state machine doesn't allow transitioning them to a terminated state.

The reconciler assumes all non-ALLOCATED instances have Ray running and attempts to transition QUEUED → RAY_STOP_REQUESTED, which is invalid.

https://github.com/ray-project/ray/blob/ba727da47a1a4af1f58c1642839deb0defd82d7a/python/ray/autoscaler/v2/instance_manager/reconciler.py#L1178-L1197

This occurs when `max_workers` configuration is dynamically reduced or when instances exceed the limit.

```
2025-12-04 06:21:55,298	INFO event_logger.py:77 -- Removing 167 nodes of type elser-v2-ingest (max number of worker nodes per type reached).
2025-12-04 06:21:55,307 - INFO - Update instance QUEUED->RAY_STOP_REQUESTED (id=e13a1528-ffd9-403b-9fd1-b54e9c2698a0, type=elser-v2-ingest, cloud_instance_id=, ray_id=): draining ray: Terminating node due to MAX_NUM_NODE_PER_TYPE: max_num_nodes=None, max_num_nodes_per_type=220
2025-12-04 06:21:55,307	INFO instance_manager.py:263 -- Update instance QUEUED->RAY_STOP_REQUESTED (id=e13a1528-ffd9-403b-9fd1-b54e9c2698a0, type=elser-v2-ingest, cloud_instance_id=, ray_id=): draining ray: Terminating node due to MAX_NUM_NODE_PER_TYPE: max_num_nodes=None, max_num_nodes_per_type=220
2025-12-04 06:21:55,307 - ERROR - Invalid status transition from QUEUED to RAY_STOP_REQUESTED
```

This PR add a valid transition `QUEUED -> TERMINATED` to allow canceling queued instances.

## Related issues
Closes #59219

author: smorrisj
body:
**Summary:**
Fixes #1735 
KaTeX symbols in sas notebooks currently do not render when exported to HTML. This PR does several things:

1. Add a quick pick menu when clicking on "Export" from the notebook to present export types (html, sas). This allows for a consistent user experience across different environments that the extension runs in (Desktop / Viya Workbench / etc). Current behavior is relying on the hosts native file picker to select the correct export type, which has usability issues in hosted environments.

2. Adds marked-katex-extension to make marked aware of katex syntax. This will ensure that marked interprets the katex symbols correctly and generates the correct html for them.

3. Updates build to pull in minified katex css and fonts. This is needed so that the generated html from step 2 has the correct styling.

**Testing:**
I created a SAS notebook file that reproduces the export bugs, and then re-exported after the above changes were implemented. Tested html export of the notebook to ensure that KaTeX symbols are rendered, both with and without SAS code that produces ODS output. For internal contributors, I can provide the notebook upon request (github does not seem to allow upload of .sasnb files on PRs 😞 )

When executing PHP coverage in PHPStorm, it can't access the result file as it is output in the PHP container.

## Reproduction procedure (bug)

1. On iTop 3.2.2

author: silentely
body:
## Summary

Add support for skipping Redis TLS certificate verification via new `REDIS_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED` environment variable, enabling connections to Redis servers using self-signed or shared certificates.

## Problem

使用 `rediss://` 连接 Redis 时，如果 Redis 服务使用自签证书或共享证书，会因 TLS 证书验证失败导致连接无法建立。

**错误表现：**
```json
{"action":"schedule_auto_cleanup_error","error":"Reached the max retries per request limit (which is 20)"}
```

连接持续重试直到达到最大次数，所有依赖 Redis 的功能（限流、Session、队列）均不可用。

**Related Issues/PRs:**
- Follow-up to #93 - Extends the Redis TLS SNI fix to support certificate verification bypass
- Related to #92 - Original Redis TLS support request
- Related to #20 / #19 - Earlier Bull Queue Redis connection fixes

## Solution

新增环境变量 `REDIS_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED`，允许用户在自签证书场景下跳过证书验证。

### Key Changes

| 文件 | 变更内容 |
|------|----------|
| `.env.example` | 新增配置项说明 |
| `src/lib/redis/client.ts` | 主 Redis 客户端支持 `rejectUnauthorized`，添加 `buildTlsConfig()` 工具函数 |
| `src/lib/log-cleanup/cleanup-queue.ts` | Bull 清理队列支持 |
| `src/lib/notification/notification-queue.ts` | Bull 通知队列支持 |
| `scripts/clear-session-bindings.ts` | Session 清理脚本支持 |
| `README.md` / `README.en.md` | 配置表格新增说明 |

## Usage

```bash
# .env 配置（仅 rediss:// 协议生效）
REDIS_URL=rediss://user:pass@host:6379
REDIS_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=false
```

### Default Behavior

- `true`（默认）：验证 TLS 证书，适用于正规 CA 签发的证书
- `false`：跳过证书验证，适用于自签证书或共享证书场景

## Testing

- [x] 本地 TypeScript 类型检查通过
- [x] 使用自签证书的 rediss:// 连接测试通过
- [x] 日志正确输出 `rejectUnauthorized` 状态

## Checklist

- [x] Code follows project conventions
- [x] Self-review completed
- [x] Documentation updated (README.md, README.en.md, .env.example)
- [x] All Redis connection points updated consistently

author: jlengelbrecht
body:
## Summary

Migrate Firecrawl from ericwong/firecrawl to trieve/firecrawl (firecrawl-simple) to resolve self-hosting issues.

## Problem

The ericwong/firecrawl image bundles all services in a single container using a "harness" approach. Despite setting `USE_DB_AUTHENTICATION=false`, the code still tries to initialize Supabase clients for blocklist/indexing features, causing startup failures:

```
Error: Supabase RR client is not configured.
Error: Port 3002 did not become available within 30000ms
```

## Solution

Use [firecrawl-simple](https://github.com/devflowinc/firecrawl-simple) which is:
- Stripped down version specifically for self-hosting
- Completely removes Supabase, Posthog, Stripe, and cloud-only dependencies
- Uses separate containers for API, Worker, and Puppeteer services
- More lightweight and stable for Kubernetes deployments

## Changes

- Replace `ericwong/firecrawl:2.7.0` with `trieve/firecrawl:v0.0.55`
- Replace Playwright sidecar with `trieve/puppeteer-service-ts:v0.0.6`
- Split deployment into 3 separate controllers (api, worker, puppeteer)
- Remove PostgreSQL dependency (not needed by firecrawl-simple)
- Update NetworkPolicy for internal service communication
- Reduce resource requests (firecrawl-simple is more lightweight)

## Testing

- [ ] Firecrawl API pod starts successfully
- [ ] Worker pod starts successfully
- [ ] Puppeteer pod starts successfully
- [ ] `/health` endpoint responds
- [ ] Test scrape endpoint works

## Notes

- firecrawl-simple only supports v1 API (v2 API removed)
- Renovate will track updates via docker annotations
- Relates to STORY-085

author: voidarchive
body:
## Summary
Adds `willReadFrequently: true` to the canvas 2D context creation to eliminate the Chrome warning and potentially improve scanning performance.

## Problem
Chrome shows this warning during QR scanning:
> Canvas2D: Multiple readback operations using getImageData are faster with the willReadFrequently attribute set to true.

## Solution
Add the `willReadFrequently: true` option when creating the canvas context in `_drawToCanvas()`.

## Browser Support
The `willReadFrequently` option is supported in all modern browsers:
- Chrome 97+
- Firefox 97+
- Safari 15.4+
- Edge 97+

For older browsers, the option is simply ignored (no breaking change).

Fixes #236
Fixes #251

author: mpryahin
body:
## Summary
Comprehensive refactoring of Justfile variables for clarity and consistency, along with improvements to the development workflow and environment configuration.

## Changes

### Variable Naming Standardization
- **Docker build**: `device` → `build-target` (clarifies Docker stage vs runtime device)
- **Ports**: `container-port` → `port` in backend Justfile (running locally, not in container)
- **Storage**: `docker-volume` → `data-dir` (clearer purpose)
- **Registry**: `images-registry` → `container-registry` (conventional naming)
- **Image**: `docker-image` → `image-name` (matches Docker terminology)
- **WebRTC ports**: Combined `webrtc-port-start`/`webrtc-port-end` → single `webrtc-ports` variable
- **Proxy args**: Renamed for consistency (`docker-build-args`, `docker-run-args`)

### Dockerfile Optimization
Hardcoded container-internal paths to reduce build-time configurability:
- `ASSET_PREFIX="/html"`
- `STATIC_FILES_DIR="/geti_prompt/html"`
- `DB_DATA_DIR="/geti_prompt/data"`
- `LOGS_DIR="/geti_prompt/logs"`

### Runtime Device Configuration
- Added `device` field to `settings.py` (reads from `DEVICE` env var)
- Backend Justfile exports `DEVICE` with cu*→cuda mapping
- Simplified `model.py` to use `settings.device` directly
- Removed `DEVICE_MAP` and `_resolve_device()` indirection

### Unified Development Workflow
**New `application/dev` recipe:**
- Runs both backend and frontend in parallel
- Accepts all configuration variables from application directory
- Variables: `port`, `device`, `enable-coturn`, `stun-server`, `coturn-port`
- Sets `PUBLIC_API_URL` for frontend automatically
- CORS set to `*` for development (local and remote access)

**Created `application/README.md`** with:
- Quick start guide
- Configuration table with defaults and options
- Usage examples for CPU/GPU/XPU/Coturn/STUN
- Local and remote access instructions

### CI/CD Updates
Updated GitHub workflows to match renamed variables:
- `distrib.yml`
- `security-scan.yml`
- `collect-license.yml`
- `collect-source.yml`

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Default (CPU, port 9100)
just application/dev

# Custom backend port
just port=8080 application/dev

# Custom UI port
just ui-port=4000 application/dev

# Custom backend and UI ports
just port=8080 ui-port=4000 application/dev

# With GPU
just device=cu126 application/dev

# With Coturn
just enable-coturn=true application/dev

# With external STUN
just stun-server="stun:stun.l.google.com:19302" application/dev

# With XPU
just device=xpu application/dev

# Combined options
just device=cu126 enable-coturn=true port=8080 ui-port=4000 application/dev

The codebase had hundreds of compilation errors from inline comments in widget arguments and invalid `.shade` usage on `Color` objects.

## Changes

### Syntax fixes (259 occurrences)
- Removed inline comments from widget arguments that broke compilation
```dart
// Before: causes syntax error
Border.all(color: context.colorScheme.surfaceVariant // was Colors.grey.shade200)

// After: compiles
Border.all(color: context.outlineVariant)
```

### Color API fixes (~50 occurrences)
- Fixed invalid `.shadeXXX` access on `Color` constants
```dart
// Before: Color doesn't have shades
color: AppColors.error.shade600

// After: use defined constants
color: AppColors.error
```

### Import additions (37 files)
- Added missing `theme_extensions.dart` for context color/text helpers
- Added missing `colors.dart` for AppColors constants

### Improved color consistency
- Replaced ambiguous `surfaceVariant` with semantic colors
- Fixed contrast issues (e.g., `warningLight` background + `warningDark` text)
- Used `outlineVariant` for borders, `textSecondary` for secondary text

- 37 files across Superadmin, Staff Tablet, POS, Builder, and Client modules
- No business logic or UI design changes

author: ayushsgithub24
body:
## Summary

This PR implements a **secure, production-grade refresh token–based authentication flow** that prevents users from being logged out when their access token expires.

The new design introduces **short-lived stateless access tokens** and **long-lived refresh tokens implemented as JWTs**, with **rotation, replay protection, and secure storage**, enabling seamless session continuation while maintaining strong security guarantees.

📄 **Detailed design & reasoning (Notion):**

[https://www.notion.so/Issue-117-Refresh-Token-Rotation-Improved-Authentication-Flow-2cd53c70405c801c94afe7c7250362ca](https://www.notion.so/Issue-117-Refresh-Token-Rotation-Improved-Authentication-Flow-2cd53c70405c801c94afe7c7250362ca?pvs=21)

## Background

Previously, users were required to re-authenticate once their access token expired.

This change introduces a **refresh token rotation mechanism**, allowing clients to transparently obtain new access tokens without re-login, while remaining resilient against token theft and replay attacks.

---

## Key Highlights

- **Access tokens**
    - Stateless JWTs
    - Short-lived (15 minutes)
    - Used for authorization only
- **Refresh tokens**
    - Implemented as **JWTs with a unique `jti`**
    - Signed with a **dedicated refresh signing key**
    - Stored **hashed** in the database (raw token is never persisted)
    - Rotated on every successful refresh
    - Reuse / replay attempts are rejected
- **Security**
    - Refresh tokens delivered via **HttpOnly, Secure cookies**
    - HTTPS enforced (including dev mode)
    - Replay protection via `jti` + DB validation
    - Old refresh tokens revoked immediately on rotation or logout
- **User experience**
    - Frontend automatically refreshes access tokens on `401`
    - No breaking changes to existing `{ token }` response contract

---

## Changes Included

### Backend

- Added `RefreshToken` entity with:
    - `jti` (`tokenId`)
    - hashed token value
    - expiry, revocation state, timestamps
- Implemented refresh token lifecycle via `RefreshTokenService`
- Refactored `AuthService` to:
    - Validate refresh JWT signature & expiry
    - Extract and verify `jti`
    - Perform rotation safely
- Enhanced `UserController`:
    - `/login` issues access + refresh tokens
    - `/refresh` rotates refresh tokens and issues new access tokens
    - `/logout` revokes refresh tokens and deletes cookie
- Introduced scheduled cleanup for expired / old revoked refresh tokens
- Updated `JwtUtil`:
    - Separate signing keys for access vs refresh tokens
    - `jti` handling for refresh tokens
- Added `JwtAuthenticationEntryPoint` for consistent `401` responses
- Updated WebSocket configuration to support HTTPS/WSS

### Frontend

- Automatic access-token refresh on `401`
- Correct handling of logout (cookie + local storage cleanup)
- Secure API calls over HTTPS
- Environment adjustments for SSL development

---

## Linked Issue

Closes #117

---

## How to Test

### Backend (Dev Mode – HTTPS)

1. Run the backend with the **dev profile**:
    
    ```bash
    SPRING_PROFILES_ACTIVE=dev ./mvnw spring-boot:run
    
    ```
    
    or via IntelliJ VM options:
    
    ```
    -Dspring.profiles.active=dev
    
    ```
    
2. Open the backend URL in your browser:
    
    ```
    https://localhost:8080
    
    ```
    
    Accept the security warning (required for Secure cookies).
    

---

### Frontend (Angular with SSL)

1. Install dependencies (if not already installed):
    
    ```bash
    npm install
    
    ```
    
2. Start the Angular dev server (SSL enabled via `package.json`):
    
    ```bash
    npm start
    
    ```
    
    This runs:
    
    ```bash
    ng serve --ssl
    
    ```
    
3. Open the frontend URL in your browser:
    
    ```
    https://localhost:4200
    
    ```
    
    Accept the HTTPS security warning.
    

---

### End-to-End Verification

1. Log in with valid credentials
2. Verify:
    - Access token is stored in `localStorage`
    - Refresh token is stored as an **HttpOnly Secure cookie**
3. Wait for the access token to expire
4. Trigger any authenticated API request
5. Confirm:
    - `/api/auth/refresh` is called automatically
    - A new access token is issued
    - The original request is retried successfully
6. Log out and verify:
    - Refresh token cookie is deleted
    - Local storage is cleared
    - User is redirected to the login page

---

### Important Notes for Local Testing

- Both **backend and frontend must be opened in the browser at least once**
- HTTPS warnings must be accepted for both origins
- Secure cookies will **not work over HTTP**

---

## Notes / Risks

- Refresh tokens are stored **hashed** in the database; raw tokens are never persisted
- Refresh token rotation introduces a database lookup during refresh
- Secure cookies require HTTPS even in development
- Local development requires manual acceptance of self-signed certificates
- Refresh token reuse or replay attempts are rejected
- No breaking changes to the frontend API contract (`{ token }` response preserved)

---

## Migration / Rollout

- No schema-breaking changes beyond adding the `refresh_token` table
- Existing users will receive refresh tokens on their next login
- Safe to roll out incrementally

author: devlin-moyer
body:
#### Main improvements in this PR:

This pull request:

- Removes reaction `rxn00375_c0`: N-Formylglutamine + H<sub>2</sub>O <=> Glutamate + Formate, GPR: `MASE_RS12045`
- Removes `rxn00552_c0`: D-Glucosamine phosphate + H<sub>2</sub>O <=> D-fructose-6-phosphate + NH<sub>3</sub>, GPR: `MASE_RS13815`
- Removes reaction `rxn01102_c0`: Glycerate + ATP --> 3-Phosphoglycerate + ADP + H<sup>+</sup>, GPR: `MASE_RS15135`
- Removes reaction `rxn01670_c0`: Nicotinamide ribonucleotide + H<sub>2</sub>O <=> N-Ribosylnicotinamide + Phosphate, GPR: `MASE_RS02790`
- Removes reaction `rxn02798_c0`: Estrone 3-sulfate + H<sub>2</sub>O <=> Estrone + Sulfate + H<sup>+</sup>, GPR: `MASE_RS16745`
- Removes reaction `rxn08599_c0`: GDP-mannose + H<sub>2</sub>O <=> D-Mannose + GDP, GPR: `MASE_RS16580`
- Removes metabolite `cpd00362_c0`: Estrone
- Removes metabolite `cpd00770_c0`: N-Formyl-glutamine
- Removes metabolite `cpd01669_c0`: Estrone-3 sulfate
- Removes metabolite `cpd02016_c0`: N-Ribosylnicotinamide
- Removes genes `MASE_RS12045`, `MASE_RS15135`, `MASE_RS16580`, and `MASE_RS16745` from the model
- Changes the GPR of `rxn00555_c0` from `MASE_RS18525` to `MASE_RS18525 or MASE_RS13815`
- Changes the GPR of `rxn00629_c0` from `MASE_RS08045` to `MASE_RS08045 or MASE_RS11295`

All of these reactions and metabolites are dead-ends, so removing them won’t affect the model’s predicted fluxes in any way. All of these were also reactions and metabolites that weren’t also in both the MIT1002 and HOT1A3 models, so removing them clarifies which differences in the three strains’ metabolism we actually have evidence for.

Neither `MASE_RS16745` nor `MASE_RS16580` were annotated with any E.C. numbers, no other genes were annotated with appropriate E.C. numbers for `rxn00375_c0` (3.1.6.1) or `rxn02798_c0` (I actually can’t find any appropriate E.C. numbers for this reaction), and no other reactions involved either estrone-3-sulfate (`cpd01669_c0`) or estrone (`cpd00362_c0`).

`MASE_RS13815` is currently the only gene in the GPR of `rxn00552_c0`, but was only annotated with the E.C. number for `rxn00555_c0` (2.6.1.16), and no genes were annotated with the E.C. number for `rxn00552_c0` (3.5.99.6). `rxn00555_c0` is already in all three strains’ models.

`MASE_RS15135` was annotated as a restriction enzyme, and no other genes were annotated with the E.C. number for `rxn01102_c0` (2.7.1.31).

`MASE_RS02790` was annotated with E.C.s 3.6.1.45 and 3.1.3.5, but [KEGG has a comment for 3.6.1.45](https://www.genome.jp/entry/3.6.1.45) saying that some but not all enzymes of this class also appear to have 5’-nucleotidase (see EC 3.1.3.5) activity”. Since N-Ribosylnicotinamide doesn’t participate in any reactions other than `rxn01670_c0`, I’m not seeing much reason to believe that `MASE_RS02790` actually has broad-specificity 5’-nucleotidase activity (i.e. can catalyze `rxn01670_c0`). `rxn01670_c0` is currently in the HOT1A3 and ATCC27126 models but not the MIT1002 model.

`MASE_RS12045` was annotated with 3.5.2.6, which is hydrolysis of β-lactams, which is definitely not what `rxn00375_c0` represents. No other genes were annotated with the appropriate E.C. number for `rxn00375_c0` (3.5.1.68), and no other reactions involve N-formylglutamine (`cpd00770_c0`).

`MASE_RS11295` is the reciprocal best BLAST hit of `WP_049589016.1`; see [MIT1002 PR #339](https://github.com/C-CoMP-STC/GEM-mit1002/pull/339).

**I hereby confirm that I have:**
- [X] Made my edits to the model on the XML file
- [ ] Tested my code on my own computer for running the model
- [X] Selected `develop` as a target branch
- [ ] Any removed reactions and metabolites have been moved to the corresponding deprecated identifier lists
